**Cached states encode context, not just token spelling.** In causal attention, a later token's hidden representation depends on earlier tokens. Change an early instruction and the same later word may produce different keys and values in subsequent layers. [1](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

For example, the suffix “answer in one sentence” following two different system contexts is textually identical but may not have the same internal states. Reusing its old KV values would compute a different model execution from a fresh forward pass.

**Only the unchanged prefix remains eligible.** Hash-chained caches reject the changed block and its descendants. Blocks strictly before the edit may still be reusable at the implementation's block granularity. An edit near the beginning therefore invalidates almost everything later, but not necessarily every cached block.

Append new information when that preserves the intended semantics, and version stable prompts deliberately. Do not keep stale states merely because an edit looks small to a human. Correct cache identity follows computational dependencies; otherwise a performance optimization silently changes the answer distribution.

**Technical details and references.**

In causal attention, a token's hidden state and later-layer KV representations depend on preceding context. Changing an early system-prompt token therefore makes the suffix's cached states inconsistent, even if all later user-visible tokens are textually unchanged. Hash-chained prefix caches naturally reject the changed block and its descendants. [1](https://docs.vllm.ai/en/latest/design/prefix_caching/) [2](https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762)

The unchanged prefix before the edit can remain reusable at the cache's block granularity; it is not necessarily the entire cache that becomes invalid. If the edit occurs near the start, almost every later block is affected, which explains the large recomputation in multi-turn workflows. Append new information when semantically appropriate and version stable prompts deliberately. Never reuse stale KV values solely because the conversation's final text looks similar or because the edit seems minor to a human.
